transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Helios Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Helios Infra), Tom Baxter (Helios Product), Ava Li (Helios Security)

Summary (auto): Demo and console walkthrough focused on migration parity from OpenAI / Anthropic / Together -> Redwood API; discussed API mappings, embedding parity, streaming & function call differences, security (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and next steps for a pilot and parity bench.

Topics: parity mapping, console tour, optimize recommendations, security/compliance, pilot scope

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Price, AE at Redwood. We'll do a quick intro then Maya will jump into the console and parity mapping.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, this is Priya. Quick note, our goal is a low-friction swap from OpenAI + Anthropic for text gen and embeddings. We mostly care about parity for our compliance docs pipeline and a Q&A product.
[00:32] Jordan: Great, and Carlos on infra?
[00:34] Carlos: Yep, Carlos here. We run a mix of cloud infra, mostly GCP, and we need VPC peering to keep traffic internal. Also KMS for key management.
[00:44] Maya: Awesome. I'll show the API compatibility shim and the console. Quick callout: Redwood's API is intentionally OpenAI-compatible in common shapes - but there are small mapping details we usually call out.
[00:58] [01:00] Maya: So starting live, here's the console. // click sounds // On the models tab you see curated variants and recommended profiles for latency/cost. For Helios you'd pick a text-gen model tuned for instruction parity.
[01:18] Tom: How do you handle function calling vs the OpenAI function call pattern? We use structured tool calling heavily.
[01:26] Maya: Good question. We support function-style calls; the JSON schema is the same shape in most cases. Note: streaming chunk boundaries are sometimes different so we recommend a short adapter in your client if you rely on exact byte offsets.
[01:44] Priya: Any differences in token counting - like how you bill or how prompts are tokenized?
[01:50] Jordan: Tokenization is model-dependent; Redwood exposes token counts in responses. Billing is per-token unit similarly, but our Optimize tool will recommend batching and KV caching to bring down per-token cost.
[02:06] [02:15] Maya: Pulling up the Optimize suggestions for a sample workload — it shows batching windows, prefix cache opportunities and a quantization recommendation. For Helios, we flagged in the analysis that many prompts reuse a short system prefix - so prefix caching alone could save ~30% of token cost.
[02:33] Carlos: When you say KV cache, do you mean the per-request KV cache? Our infra team worried about stale caches across replicas.
[02:41] Maya: Right - the KV cache is per model instance but Redwood's serving runtime has a cache-coherency protocol and TTL controls. Small chance the transcript might say K V catch, but that's just the ASR.
[02:56] [03:00] Priya: Ok, let's talk parity for Anthropic - we use Claude for some safety filtering workflows. Is Redwood compatible?
[03:08] Jordan: We don't replicate Claude's safety stack 1:1. We map prompts and system messages and then run a post-processing safety policy; for high compliance use cases we recommend your existing safety layer stay in-line or we can integrate via a webhook flow.
[03:24] Ava: On security, can you summarize network boundary options? VPC, private deployment, dedicated?
[03:31] Jordan: Sure - three main modes: Hosted (public API with encryption in transit), Dedicated (reserved capacity with network controls), and Private (VPC/air-gapped on-prem). For Helios we usually recommend Dedicated or Private for finance. We also integrate with KMS/HSM.
[03:49] [04:00] Maya: Showing the private deployment config in the console - you can pin a model version, set rollout policies, and configure a canary with automatic fallback to a cheaper variant.
[04:15] Tom: How do rollouts handle schema changes or prompt differences? We've had issues when models produce slightly different structured outputs.
[04:22] Maya: We have an eval harness tied to your prompt set; you can run pre-rollout tests that check structural regexes and value ranges. If the canary fails, traffic automatically rolls back.
[04:36] [04:45] Priya: On the evals side, does Redwood host our prompts or do they stay in our environment?
[04:50] Jordan: By default we store evals metadata in the control plane for analysis, but for sensitive content we can keep the evaluation dataset in your VPC and run the harness locally in Private mode.
[05:03] [05:15] Carlos: For the pilot we need to know expected latency at our 99th percentile. Can you share SLO numbers?
[05:22] Maya: Typical p99 depends on model/sequence length. For the family of models we recommend, p99 at 1k tokens is usually ~600-900ms on dedicated instances; hosted will vary by region. We'll run a parity bench to give you numbers with your prompts.
[05:38] [05:45] Jordan: Also worth flagging our smart routing: if a region is overloaded your traffic can route to a cheaper/compatible variant; that's configurable by policy.
[05:56] Tom: Any functional differences with Together models? We sometimes use Together for high-throughput internal inference.
[06:02] Maya: Together models can map similarly; the main differences are tokenization and recommended quantization. Our Optimize tool will recommend an int8 or int4 quantization profile depending on your quality tolerance.
[06:15] [06:30] Priya: Do you support embeddings parity? We have an existing vector index built on embeddings from OpenAI.
[06:38] Maya: Yes, embeddings are supported. The embedding vector dimensionality might vary between models; for parity you can pick a Redwood-verified embedding model that matches dimensionality or run a conversion layer. We also have a helper script to re-index with minimal downtime.
[06:58] Ava: About compliance artifacts - can you produce SOC2 report, network diagrams, and a data flow diagram?
[07:05] Jordan: Yes, we can supply SOC2 type II summary, network diagrams, and a security pack. We'll attach those docs. Also our KMS integrations are logged in audit trails visible in the console.
[07:18] [07:30] Carlos: How do you handle request logs retention and egress for PII?
[07:36] Maya: Logs are configurable. For Private mode logs can stay in your VPC. For hosted, logs are retained per your retention policy and can be redacted. We have redaction hooks and token-level cost breakdown.
[07:50] [08:00] Jordan: Quick demo of an API call - here's a sample node snippet that mirrors the OpenAI chat completion shape. Note the minor differences: model name prefix, and we return a token_count field on the response. // shows code //
[08:22] [08:30] Tom: That looks easy. Do you preserve message role semantics? We use system/user/assistant heavily.
[08:36] Maya: Yes. Role semantics are preserved. The one thing to watch is function call resolution timing - the assistant might return the function name earlier or streaming partials which your orchestration might need to handle.
[08:53] [09:00] Priya: For parity bench, what metrics will you measure?
[09:05] Maya: We'll measure latency (p50/p95/p99), token cost, output similarity (BLEU/ROUGE-ish plus human spot checks), structured output pass-rate for your regen tests, and throughput at concurrency.
[09:19] [09:30] Jordan: We'll also provide a cost estimate: projected per-token spend based on your historical token counts and our batching/Optimize recommendations.
[09:36] Carlos: If we do Dedicated, are there minimums or reserved commitments?
[09:41] Jordan: Yes Dedicated has monthly commitments. We can size a 3-month pilot if you want to avoid long-term commits while we validate parity.
[09:52] [10:00] Tom: Are there any gotchas migrating our embeddings index? We run a FAISS cluster.
[10:06] Maya: Migration path: export vectors, choose a matching embedding model or re-embed, then backfill index. We provide scripts and the Console has a reindexing job monitor that supports low-impact backfills.
[10:20] [10:30] Priya: A few quick questions from my ML team - how deterministic are outputs given the same seed/temperature?
[10:36] Maya: Determinism depends on model internals and tokenization. We support seeding for some model families; if strict determinism is required we recommend pinned model versions and a controlled runtime (Dedicated/Private).
[10:50] [11:00] Ava: Security question - do you integrate with SSO and RBAC? We need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[11:06] Jordan: Yes SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM are supported. RBAC roles are configurable in the Console and audit trails are available for all API keys.
[11:18] [11:30] Carlos: For the bench, we'll provide a 2k-prompt sample and traffic pattern file. Anything else you need?
[11:34] Maya: That should be enough. Also send a sample of your function call payloads if you use structured tooling heavily.
[11:44] [11:50] Jordan: Recap and next steps: we'll share sandbox creds & quickstart, Maya will run parity bench, Helios to share compliance questionnaire and traffic sample, and we'll reconvene for pilot kickoff.
[12:02] Priya: Sounds good. Any cost ballpark?
[12:06] Jordan: We'll include a ballpark in the follow-up; Optimize suggestions will show bottom-line impact. Expect material savings if you adopt prefix caching and batching.
[12:18] [12:30] Tom: Thanks all. Looks promising.
[12:34] Ava: Thanks. We'll review security docs when received.
[12:38] Jordan: Great, I'll send the pack. Thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
